Azo compounds, diazo compounds, and hydrazines all contain nitrogen-nitrogen bonds and are known to be potentially unstable. When these compounds are mixed with oxidizing acids (like nitric acid, perchloric acid, etc.), they can undergo rapid oxidation reactions.

The main hazard associated with mixing these nitrogen-containing compounds with oxidizing acids is explosion. These combinations can lead to extremely rapid decomposition reactions that release large amounts of gas and energy in a very short time, resulting in explosive reactions.

This is because:
1. Azo compounds (R-N=N-R') contain N=N bonds that can be oxidized rapidly
2. Diazo compounds (R-N₂) are already unstable and can decompose explosively
3. Hydrazines (R-NH-NH-R') are strong reducing agents that react violently with oxidizers
